newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to invest $477 mln in Kokomo plants.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to invest $477 mln in Kokomo plants.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Monday it will invest $477 million in a five-year modernization program at the Kokomo Transmission and Casting plants and hire an additional 784 workers in the Kokomo, Indiana area over the next-two-and-a-half years.
The additional investment, along with the 1995 plan to build the Indiana Transmission Plant, will bring recent investments in the Kokomo area to more than $1.5 billion.
The state of Indiana will provide an additional $750,000 training grant to Chrysler, adding to a $1 million training grant announced two years ago, the company said.

The new workers will build transmissions at the existing Kokomo Transmission Plant and the new Indiana Transmission Plant. The Indiana Transmission Plant will begin production of new fully-electronic automatic transmissions in the summer of 1998.
Chrysler said the Indiana Transmission plant will be staffed by a combination of transfers from the Kokomo Transmission Plant and new employees.
The Kokomo Transmission plant will remain fully-operational with current and future products, Chrysler said. There are presently 7,400 employees at the three Howard County plants.
